name: JOSM
description: App update notify-only, but the plugin manager downloads plugin jars with zero hash/signature (only checks it's a valid jar) — content-as-code.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: JOSM’s reviewed plugin component checks JAR readability. That structural check does not establish publisher authentication or classify the core application updater.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study checkout; the cited evidence is limited to plugin downloads and does not establish the core application updater's notification behavior or release signing.

original_evidence.text: | JOSM | https://github.com/openstreetmap/josm | 331d9b3 / 2026-08-19 | N (main app, notify-only); **Y** (plugin system) | N (manual, user-triggered) | **Y (plugins)** | HTTPS (`Config.getUrls().getJOSMWebsite()` default is https) | N (no manifest signing) | **none** | **none** | `src/org/openstreetmap/josm/plugins/PluginDownloadTask.java:105-153` downloads a plugin jar from `pi.downloadlink` (http/https) with **no hash/signature check**; `PluginHandler.installDownloadedPlugins()` (`src/org/openstreetmap/josm/plugins/PluginHandler.java:1407-1468`) only verifies the file `is a valid JAR` (`new JarFile(updatedPlugin).close()`) before renaming `.jar.new`→`.jar` and loading it — no checksum/signature field exists anywhere in `PluginInformation.java`. Main JOSM app itself is notify-only (`src/org/openstreetmap/josm/gui/bugreport/JosmUpdatePanel.java` just prompts the user to visit the download page) |
